chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Misma'i, who said:

When Dawud ibn Ali killed Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I will surely supplicate to Allah against the one who killed my master and took my wealth.' So Dawud ibn Ali said to him: 'You are threatening me with your supplication?'

Hammad said: Al-Misma'i said: 'Mo'tab narrated to me that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) did not cease being in Ruku' and Sajdah throughout his night. So when it was in the pre-dawn hours, I heard him saying while he was in Sajdah: 'O Allah! I ask You by Your Strong Power and by Your Intense Majesty, which all Your creation is humble before, that You send Salat upon Muhammad and the People of his Household, and that You seize him at the moment, at the moment.'

So he had not raised his head until we heard the shriek in the house of Dawud ibn Ali. So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) raised his head and said: 'I supplicated to Allah with a supplication, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent an Angel upon him, so he struck his head with an iron sledgehammer, his bladder split from it, so he died.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ بَيْتِهِ: The People of his Household (Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.السَّحَرِ: The pre-dawn hours, a time of accepted supplication
key_terms.الْمُعَلَّى بْنُ خُنَيْسٍ: Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.دَاوُدُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: Dawud ibn Ali, a prominent figure in early Shia history
key_terms.رَاكِعاً وَ سَاجِداً: In bowing and prostration, referring to continuous prayer

ai.seo_question: What happened to Dawud ibn Ali after Imam al-Sadiq supplicated against him?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the spiritual authority of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) through the mechanism of *Du'a al-Munajat*, where his prolonged night prayer directly precipitated the sudden, violent death of the Umayyad governor Dawud ibn Ali. The specific detail of the angel striking Dawud with an iron sledgehammer (*mirzaba*) serves as a divine punishment for the injustice committed against the Imam's companion, Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays. This event underscores the Shia belief in the efficacy of the Imams' supplications to alter worldly affairs and exact retribution against oppressors.
